structure_note: 62 pages, all with OCR, only 33 translated; page 48 carries a refusal placeholder instead of a translation. No printed page numbers. The OCR on three of four sampled pages ends in a repetition loop, so the 'translated' count overstates readable text.

reader_summary: A Hangul manuscript of conduct instruction for women (the sampled page 7 is headed as its postface). On three of four sampled pages the transcription is not this leaf's text: it loops one word or one paragraph, and the English renders the loop and invents a 'calligraphy practice' story to explain it. Neither pane can be trusted.
book_verdict: Cursive vernacular Korean defeated the lite OCR: repetition loops and confabulated text on 3/4 pages, carried into fluent English with invented explanations. Needs re-OCR by a capable reader before anyone sees it.

reader_summary: A Korean manuscript anthology of model examination compositions in Classical Chinese, on topics from Zhou to Ming history. The transcription is of the right text but has misreadings, and on dense parallel-prose pages it breaks down into strings of single characters. The English is loose and sometimes turns phrases into invented people (title of p.13) or covers garbled OCR with fluent prose (p.95).
book_verdict: Real and interesting exam-composition anthology; topic lists read acceptably, but the dense parallel prose is weakly transcribed and the English invents names and sense. Show only with a warning that the English is a rough draft.

title: Tʻonggam chu, Sŏhan chi odae
shelf_note: Korean manuscript glossary to the Zizhi tongjian (Western Han to Five Dynasties); headwords with small glosses and red dynasty labels (西漢, 唐). Text is Classical Chinese though language says Korean.
structure_note: 126 pages, 118 translated. Printed backsteps (3) and repeats (9) most likely come from misread leaf numerals or year headwords taken as page numbers, not from a disorder I could see; the sampled pages run in order (Han → Jin → Tang). Page 23 is heavily overwritten with large brush characters over the glossary, which makes it largely unreadable.

reader_summary: A Korean manuscript glossary of words and names from the Comprehensive Mirror (Zizhi tongjian), headword plus short gloss, arranged by dynasty. The transcription is of the right leaves but misreads many headwords and on one overwritten leaf invents glosses; the English treats the glossary as prose and turns words into invented people and places.
book_verdict: A real reader's aid to the Tongjian, but the OCR misreads headwords and the English invents names (Su Che, 'Zheng Yu', 'Cui Mang'). Useful as images with the Chinese text as a rough finding aid; the English should not be relied on.

title: Sinpʻyŏn Sanhak kyemong

structure_note: 168 pages, 167 with OCR, 154 translated. Printed numbers (17 read, 4 backsteps) are sparse; page 81 carries a leaf number (三九) correctly, so the backsteps are most likely misread numerals. OCR self-tags pages 38 and 124 as 'printed'; they are handwritten (O16, minor).

reader_summary: A Korean manuscript copy of Zhu Shijie's Suanxue qimeng, the Yuan arithmetic primer studied in Joseon. The transcription is of the right text and the English follows the method sentences well, but numbers are often wrong or missing in both panes: answers, small-type totals and fractions. A reader cannot check a problem against the English without the image.
book_verdict: Right work, clear handwriting, and the method prose is translated well, but numerals are misread or dropped on every sampled page, which in a mathematics book is the content. Show only with a warning to check every figure against the image.
